verified.exploit_entry_point: Cosmos messages dispatched through the application's real MsgServiceRouter (app/apptesting KeeperTestHelper.RunMsg). This is the same router that CosmWasm stargate dispatch, authz MsgExec inner messages and ICA-host messages call; it deliberately does not run the ante handler, so it reproduces every route that skips the transaction-level IID check. Every security test seeds the real on-chain state (DID documents via IidKeeper.SetDidDocument, bonds/batches, entities, collections, claims) and asserts the protected balance or record is unchanged, or that a legitimate request still succeeds.
variants: T1 payer-account binding: the handler resolves the account out of the DID document for a fragment supplied by the request. Both the direct case (the fragment names a victim's key) and the producer case (the attacker's own document registers a verification method whose blockchain account id is the victim's account) reproduce; only the second needs the resolved account compared with the signer.

T2 entity keeper binding: the entity DID lists a controller DID, and the keeper checks DID-controls-DID, but never binds the request's signer to that controller DID; UpdateEntity and UpdateEntityVerified mutate entity state.

T3 bond DID equality: EditBond, UpdateBondState, SetNextAlpha and WithdrawReserve compare a stored DID with a DID supplied in the request; the supplied DID is a plain field and the signer is never bound to it.
T4 injected sibling (dispute deposit): the dispute deposit is funded from the account registered on the named DID's document; a document controlled by the attacker can register another account.

T5 injected sibling (reserve withdrawal fee): the exit fee is debited from the account the withdrawer DID resolves to; the bond's stored controller DID equality passes even when the fragment resolves elsewhere.
verified.project_tests_run: Functional group: the project's own tests for ./x/bonds/keeper, ./x/claims/keeper, ./x/entity/keeper, ./x/iid/ante, ./x/entity/ante and ./app/apptesting, restored from the agent's tree and run with the native Go runner. Three upstream tests assert the pre-fix authorisation model (a message acts for a DID with no controller key present) and are skipped by name: TestKeeperTestSuite/TestMsgEditBond, TestKeeperTestSuite/TestMsgEditBond_WrongEditor, TestKeeperTestSuite/TestMsgUpdateBondState_AugmentedHatchToOpen and TestKeeperTestSuite/TestMsgUpdateEntity. All other project tests in those packages pass at pinned+injected, on the oracle and on every patch variant. `go build ./...` is clean at pinned+injected on the host (Go 1.27.2); the image uses Go 1.22.
verified.hidden_counts: 12 security tests fail at pinned+injected and pass on the oracle; 11 hidden functional tests pass on both; the project test packages above add the remainder of the functional group.

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected operation changes balances or stored records; the module queries are read-only and do not act for a DID, so there is no read path to leave unguarded
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: DID fragments are opaque identifiers; the fixed paths resolve them to canonical bech32 accounts and compare those, so a malformed spelling fails to resolve (fails closed) instead of slipping past the guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: authorization is derived from on-chain DID state, not from an external authority response that could be empty or absent

traps.shape: a handler resolves the account to debit out of the DID document named by a request field; a DID document may register any blockchain account as a verification method, so checking that the signer controls the DID passes while the debit lands on another account; only binding the resolved account to the signer's own address closes it
traps.where: x/bonds/keeper/msg_server.go:692 MakeOutcomePayment, :431 Buy, :503 performFirstSwapperFunctionBuy, :628 Swap, :735 WithdrawShare
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the transaction-level IID check already binds the signer to the DID, and the handler derives the payer from the DID document, so the request looks authorised
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the keeper authorises DID-controls-DID (the entity lists the controller DID) and the relayer DID pinned in entity state, but never binds the request's signer to that DID
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the controller DID must control the entity DID, and the relayer DID must equal the one stored on the entity, so both look like existing authorization
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; the published fix adds the same in-keeper binding to these two handlers

traps.shape: the stored DID is compared with a DID supplied in the request, but that DID is only a field: nothing proves the signer controls it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the handler already compares the caller's DID with the bond's creator/controller/oracle DID, so it reads as an authorization check
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; the published fix closed the whole module with a kill switch rather than these handlers

traps.shape: injected sibling: the dispute deposit is funded from the account the named DID document registers, so a document the signer controls can register another account and the deposit leaves the other account
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the deposit is described as held against the disputer's DID, the request already carries a disputer DID and address, and the deposit is the caller's own stake
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a maintainer could plausibly tie the stake to the disputer's DID document

traps.shape: injected sibling: the reserve-withdrawal exit fee is debited from the account the withdrawer DID resolves to; the stored controller DID equality passes, and a document registering another account makes the fee come from that account
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the withdrawal is already gated by the bond controller DID equality and the amount check, and the fee is charged to the withdrawer's DID account
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: an exit fee charged to the withdrawer's DID account
